notes_list.title: Peptide Bond and Protein-Level Chemistry
notes_list.basic_overview: A peptide bond is an amide linkage formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and amino group of another, with resonance giving partial double-bond character.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Restricted rotation and planarity arise from amide resonance. N→C direction is used for peptide sequence notation.
notes_list.examples: Dipeptide formation, hydrolysis under acidic/basic conditions, and peptide mapping.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Biological peptide synthesis uses activated intermediates/enzymatic coupling; hydrolysis can be acid/base catalyzed.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: amine attacks activated carboxyl derivative; tetrahedral intermediate forms; leaving group departs. Direct condensation of free amino acids is less favorable without activation.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Amide hydrolysis has a significant activation barrier and is accelerated by strong acid/base or enzymes.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Connect organic amide chemistry to biomolecules.
notes_list.common_traps: Peptide bond is planar; do not treat it like a freely rotating single C–N bond.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
